to aid in testing the next round of improvements for Dogecoin Core.
Dogecoin Core, Dogecoin's reference implementation, is the software most commonly used to run a Dogecoin node.
In separate posts, 'Junior Developer' sought contributors for both documentation and software testing in two help requests.

One request calls for native Japanese speakers to review a proposed documentation change in Dogecoin Core. No development experience is required, opening the testing effort to community members who can help ensure the documentation is accurate and natural for Japanese-speaking users.

"Help wanted: native Japanese speakers to review a proposed documentation change in Dogecoin Core. No development experience required," Junior Developer wrote alongside a GitHub pull request document that invites contributors to add their language by creating a folder, placing the translated file there, and linking it from the index. Japanese was one of the languages still missing, so this adds it.

The second call asks for developers on the latest macOS release to help test a small header guard improvement proposal in Dogecoin Core: "Help wanted: developers on the latest macOS release to test a small header guard improvement proposal in Dogecoin Core."
Help wanted: developers on the newest Mac OS release to test a small header guard improvement proposal in Dogecoin Core:https://t.co/vLSTKBzJuX

Both calls emphasize the need for community testing in Dogecoin's open-source development process. Rather than limiting testing to core contributors, developers are asking users and programmers with relevant language or operating-system experience to help identify potential issues before changes move forward.
Dogecoin developers continue building, with behind-the-scenes activity culminating in a major improvement and achievement for the network.

The Dogecoin Foundation's team successfully conducted an experimental post-quantum secure transaction on Dogecoin's mainnet in April 2026, in line with the crypto industry's continuing efforts to build quantum resilience following Google's research update at the end of March 2026.
In January 2025, Dogecoin developers proposed a next-generation quantum-resistant encryption system called RE-EN (Revolutionary Encryption Network) for Dogecoin's security infrastructure.

title: Dogecoin Developer Turns to Community for Next Core Upgrade Tests
